Target models

targets.Rd

The target is the model your center fits to its own data. Every target can borrow from an external release through cv.bregsurv(); what changes between targets is the likelihood the integration weight is balanced against.

Usage

target_cox(
  time,
  event,
  z,
  stratum = NULL,
  ties = c("none", "breslow", "exact"),
  score = "linear"
)

target_ncc(case, set, z)

target_discrete(
  interval,
  event,
  z,
  stratum = NULL,
  link = c("cloglog", "logit"),
  n_intervals = NULL,
  score = "linear"
)

Arguments

time

Observed times.

event

Event indicator (1 = event, 0 = censored).

z

Covariate matrix or data frame, one row per subject, with column names.

stratum

Optional stratum labels; each stratum has its own baseline.

ties

Tie handling for target_cox(): "none", "breslow" or "exact".

score

"linear" or an nn_score() specification.

case

Case indicator for target_ncc() (1 = case, 0 = control).

set

Matched-set identifier for target_ncc().

interval

Integer interval index 1, ..., K of each subject's last interval at risk.

link

Link of the linear discrete-time model: "cloglog" (grouped proportional hazards) or "logit". The neural discrete-time model always uses the logit (logistic-hazard) link.

n_intervals

Number of intervals K; defaults to max(interval).

Value

An object of class "bregsurv_target".

Details

  • target_cox() is the stratified Cox model, scored by its log-partial likelihood. Tied event times are handled by ties: "none" (the default), "breslow", or "exact" (Kullback-Leibler divergence only).

  • target_ncc() is the nested case-control (matched case-control) design: the conditional likelihood of which member of each matched set is the case.

  • target_discrete() is the grouped-time model of a discrete outcome: subject i is at risk in intervals 1, ..., interval[i] and the event, if any, happens in interval[i]. The interval hazard is \(h_{k}(z) = g^{-1}(\gamma_{sk} + z^\top\beta)\) with a complementary log-log (grouped proportional hazards, the default) or logit link and one baseline parameter per stratum and interval.

With score = nn_score(...), the risk score of the Cox target, or the interval hazards of the discrete target, are given by a neural network instead of a linear predictor (requires the torch package).

See also

release_coef(), cv.bregsurv()

Examples

data(ExampleData_lowdim)
tr <- ExampleData_lowdim$train
tg <- target_cox(time = tr$time, event = tr$status, z = tr$z)
tg
#> Target: Cox model, linear risk score
#>   100 subjects, 6 covariates, 29 events
